title: 1. Relational database model
description: Tuples, relation properties, degree and cardinality, business rules, and fundamental relational algebra operators. Meaning of NULL values.

items.question: What is a tuple?
items.explanation: A tuple is one row in a relation. For example, (100, 'Matthew') gives the SID and SName values for one student. Week 2 uses the term on page 27 but does not define it there.
items.explanationImageAlt: A STUDENT relation with one highlighted row labelled Tuple: one record's attribute values.

references.label: Week 2 related reading, p. 27
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: A relation has 12 rows and 4 columns. What are its degree and cardinality, respectively?
items.explanation: Degree counts columns (4); cardinality counts rows (12). These are standard relational-model terms; the linked slide provides background on tables, not these definitions.

references.label: Week 2: Relational databases, p. 22
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 2 - Data Model & Relational Database Model 7 Oct 2026 StuVer.pdf

items.question: Which is a business rule?

options.text: Each order must belong to exactly one user.

items.explanation: A business rule constrains valid data. For example, order 101 must identify one user; an order with no user would violate this rule.

references.label: Week 2: Business rules, p. 10

items.question: Which relational algebra operator filters rows?
items.explanation: Relational-algebra SELECT keeps rows that satisfy a condition. For example, selecting SID = 100 keeps only rows for that student. In SQL, WHERE performs this filtering.

references.label: Week 7: Relational set operators, p. 6
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: In relational algebra, which operator keeps only the SID and SName columns of STUDENT?
items.explanation: PROJECT keeps the named attributes. For example, projecting SID and SName from STUDENT(SID, SName, Phone) leaves out Phone.

references.label: Week 7: Relational set operators, p. 6
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: Two compatible one-column relations contain student IDs: A = {100, 200, 300} and B = {200, 400}. Which relational-algebra expression returns {100, 300}?
items.explanation: A DIFFERENCE B keeps rows in A but not in B. The shared ID 200 is removed; 400 was never in A.

references.label: Week 7: Relational set operators, p. 6
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: NULL values: What can you conclude from the NULL in John’s Phone No. column?

options.text: John has a phone number but chose not to share it.
John does not have a phone number.
No phone number is recorded for John, and the table does not tell us why.

items.explanation: NULL represents a missing value, not zero. John’s number could be unknown, deliberately withheld, or not applicable. For example, a number not yet entered and a number withheld for privacy can both appear as NULL.
